context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Numbers 30:1–16.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Vows made void by a father or husband are followed by repeated statements that the LORD will forgive the woman.
observations.label: Voided vows are followed by forgiveness: action

payload.posture: Read Numbers 30:1–16 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: Vows made void by a father or husband are followed by repeated statements that the LORD will forgive the woman.
payload.title: Voided vows are followed by forgiveness
